claim: The second postnatal week is a critical stage for synapse formation in the rodent neocortex.
source: Given that the second postnatal week is a critical stage for synapse formation in the rodent neocortex (Lendvai et al., 2000; Holtmaat and Svoboda, 2009), we chose postnatal day 11 (P11) as the time point for our examination.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Lendvai et al., 2000; Holtmaat and Svoboda, 2009).

claim: 6505 neurons were collected from an initial pool of 17,438 cells after cluster analysis.
source: After the cluster analysis (Figure 1—figure supplements 2–4), we collected 6505 neurons from an initial pool of 17,438 cells (Figure 1A, Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by data from the cluster analysis and referenced figures showing the cell selection process.

claim: C-type isoforms C3, C4, and C5 are expressed near-ubiquitously in neocortical neurons.
source: We observed the near-ubiquitous expression of 'C-type' isoforms, specifically C3, C4, and C5 (Figure 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The fraction of cells expressing C-type isoforms was significantly higher compared to variable isoforms.
source: It is important to note that the fraction of cells expressing 'C-type' isoforms was significantly higher when compared to 'variable' isoforms (Figure 1D, Figure 1—figure supplement 1E), which is consistent with findings from a previous study (Toyoda et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in figures and is consistent with a cited previous study (Toyoda et al., 2014).

claim: The majority of neocortical neurons from all clusters exhibited very low similarity level in γ-PCDH variable isoform expression patterns.
source: This extensive analysis revealed that the majority of neocortical neurons from all clusters exhibited very low similarity level (Figure 1E, Figure 1—figure supplements 5 and 6).
evidence: The claim is supported by pairwise analysis data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: Distinct combinatorial expression patterns exist among neocortical neurons.
source: This finding strongly suggests distinct combinatorial expression patterns among these neurons.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the low similarity level analysis results.

claim: A subtle but significant co-occurrence of γ-PCDH isoform expression exists in most neurons.
source: This analysis uncovered a subtle but significant co-occurrence of γ-PCDH isoform expression in most neurons (Figure 1G).
evidence: The claim is supported by variance analysis data shown in Figure 1G.

claim: Cluster 0 displayed considerably lower γ-PCDH expression and no co-occurrence of γ-PCDH isoforms.
source: Notably, we did not detect any discernible differences among clusters, except for cluster 0, which displayed considerably lower expression (Figure 1C) and no co-occurrence of γ-PCDH isoforms (Figure 1G, Figure 1—figure supplement 7).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: Pcdhg conditional knockout mice were created by crossing Pcdhg fcon3/fcon3 mice with Neurod6-cre mice.
source: These genetically engineered mice were created by crossing Pcdhg fcon3/fcon3 mice (Lefebvre et al., 2008; Prasad et al., 2008) with Neurod6-cre mice (Goebbels et al., 2006).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations describing the mouse lines used.

claim: The genetic combination of Pcdhg fcon3/fcon3 and Neurod6-cre specifically removed all variable and C-type γ-PCDH isoforms in pyramidal neurons.
source: This genetic combination specifically removed all variable and C-type γ-PCDH isoforms in pyramidal neurons.
evidence: The claim describes the experimental design and expected outcome based on the genetic manipulation.

claim: The percentage of connected pairs was notably higher in Pcdhg cKO mice (20.2%, 103/511) than in wild-type mice (15.0%, 122/813).
source: Overall, our analysis revealed that the percentage of connected pairs was notably higher in Pcdhg cKO mice (20.2%, 103/511) than in wild-type (WT) mice (15.0%, 122/813) (Figure 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiological recording data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: In Pcdhg cKO mice, a more significant difference in connectivity was observed for vertically aligned cells compared to horizontally aligned cells.
source: In Pcdhg cKO mice, we observed a more significant difference in connectivity for vertically aligned cells (18.3%, 94/515 in Pcdhg cKO mice vs. 11.2%, 73/651 in WT mice for vertically aligned neuron pairs; 12.2%, 27/221 in Pcdhg cKO mice vs. 9.5%, 28/294 in WT mice for horizontally aligned neuron pairs) (Figure 2C).
evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiological recording data comparing vertically and horizontally aligned neurons shown in Figure 2C.

claim: In Pcdha cKO mice, no significant difference in connectivity was observed compared to WT mice.
source: In these mice lacking α-PCDH, we did not observe a significant difference (11.3%, 38/337 in Pcdha cKO mice vs. 14.3%, 26/182 in WT mice, Figure 2D).
evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiological recording data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The absence of γ-PCDH expression significantly increased synapse formation between cells separated vertically by 50–100 μm.
source: A more detailed analysis of synaptic connections among vertically aligned neurons in Pcdhg cKO mice unveiled that the absence of γ-PCDH expression significantly increased synapse formation between cells separated vertically by 50–100 μm (24.0%, 50/208 in Pcdhg cKO mice vs. 9.6%, 20/208 in WT mice) (Figure 2E).
evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiological recording data analyzing distance-dependent connectivity shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Increased synapse formation in Pcdhg cKO mice was detected starting from P10 and persisted up to P20.
source: Notably, this increased synapse formation was detected starting from P10 (16.1%, 32/199 in Pcdhg cKO mice vs. 8.7%, 20/230 in WT mice for P10–12; 21.6%, 22/102 in Pcdhg cKO mice vs. 12.8%, 29/227 in WT mice for P13–15). These time points correspond to the period when chemical synapses between cortical neurons become detectable, and this trend persisted throughout our measurements, spanning up to P20 (Figure 2F).
evidence: The claim is supported by developmental profiling data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: γ-PCDHs may play a role in preventing synapse formation from the early stages of neural development.
source: Hence, our findings suggest that γ-PCDHs may play a role in preventing synapse formation from the early stages of neural development.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the developmental profiling data showing increased connectivity in knockout mice from early postnatal stages.

claim: qRT-PCR assays confirmed that electroporated isoforms exhibited significantly higher expression levels compared to non-overexpressed ones from the contralateral side.
source: The qRT-PCR assays unequivocally confirmed that the electroporated isoforms, as opposed to the non-overexpressed ones from the contralateral side, exhibited significantly higher expression levels (Figure 3A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 3A and B.

claim: Each positive neuron expressed an average of 5.6 types of isoforms after electroporation with multiple plasmids.
source: Employing a probability analysis based on the occurrence of yellow and red-only cells within the total electroporated neuron population (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B), we ascertained that each positive neuron expressed an average of 5.6 types of isoforms (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C and the top panel of Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by probability analysis data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: Single-cell RT-PCR analysis detected an average of 5.3 types out of the six electroporated isoforms from 19 neurons.
source: This result harmonized with data obtained from single-cell RT-PCR analysis, wherein an average of 5.3 types out of the six electroporated isoforms was detected from 19 neurons (Figure 3C and D and the bottom panel of Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by single-cell RT-PCR data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: Overexpressing γ-PCDH isoforms did not induce any alterations in cell positioning within the neocortex compared to control plasmids.
source: Remarkably, we observed that overexpressing γ-PCDH isoforms did not induce any alterations in cell positioning within the neocortex compared to the control plasmids (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E and F).
evidence: The claim is supported by cell distribution analysis data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: Overexpressing one or six γ-PCDH variable isoforms in neurons significantly diminished the rate of synaptic connections among them.
source: Intriguingly, overexpressing one or six γ-PCDH variable isoforms in neurons significantly diminished the rate of synaptic connections among them (10.3%, 15/146 in expressing control plasmids; 1.9%, 4/216 in overexpressing one isoform; and 4.4%, 8/181 in overexpressing six isoforms, red bars in Figure 3E).
evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiological recording data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Overexpressing γ-PCDH C4 did not have any significant effect on the synaptic connection rate.
source: However, when overexpressing γ-PCDH C4, we did not observe any significant effect on the synaptic connection rate (11.3%, 12/106 in neurons overexpressing γ-PCDH C4, Figure 3E).
evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiological recording data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Overexpression of six variable isoforms led to a reduction in the connection rate in Pcdhg cKO mice.
source: Remarkably, this overexpression also led to a reduction in the connection rate in Pcdhg cKO mice (6.1%, 12/198 in overexpressing six isoforms vs. 16.5%, 31/188 in expressing control plasmids), mirroring the outcome observed in WT littermate mice (6.6%, 8/121 in overexpressing six isoforms vs. 16.5%, 18/109 in expressing control plasmids) (Figure 3F).
evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiological recording data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: Overexpressing the variable isoforms, as opposed to the C-type isoform C4, leads to a decrease in synaptic connectivity within the mouse neocortex.
source: These compelling observations collectively underscore that overexpressing the variable isoforms, as opposed to the C-type isoform C4, leads to a decrease in synaptic connectivity within the mouse neocortex.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the combined results of overexpression experiments with variable and C-type isoforms.

claim: In the group characterized by a 100% similarity level, the connectivity rate between neurons with different colors was significantly lower compared to the control.
source: In the group characterized by a 100% similarity level, the connectivity rate between neurons with different colors that were electroporated on different days was also significantly lower compared to the control (3.7%, 5/134 in the complete-overlap group; 12.5%, 19/151 in control pairs, 100% in Figure 4D).
evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiological recording data from sequential electroporation experiments shown in Figure 4D.

claim: As the similarity levels descended from 100% to 0%, the connectivity probabilities progressively reverted to the control level.
source: However, as the similarity levels descended from 100% to 0%, the connectivity probabilities progressively reverted to the control level. The likelihood rebounded to 8.4% (14/165) for the pairs with a 33% similarity level and 10.3% (12/117) and 10.5% (12/114) for pairs with 11% or 0% similarity level, respectively (Figure 4D).
evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiological recording data showing the relationship between similarity level and connectivity shown in Figure 4D.

claim: It is the similarity level of γ-PCDH isoforms shared between neurons, rather than the absolute expression of the protein within individual neurons, that dictates the regulation of synaptic formation.
source: This compelling observation illuminated a fundamental principle: it is the similarity level of γ-PCDH isoforms shared between neurons, rather than the absolute expression of the protein within individual neurons, that dictates the regulation of synaptic formation.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the sequential electroporation experiments showing that connectivity depends on similarity level rather than absolute expression.

claim: No significant changes were observed in the synaptic connectivity between electroporated neurons and nearby control neurons.
source: Remarkably, in line with the single-electroporation experiment (gray bars in Figure 3E), no significant changes were observed in the synaptic connectivity between electroporated neurons and nearby control neurons (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiological recording data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: There is a discernible negative correlation between the probability of synaptic connections and the similarity level of γ-PCDH isoforms expressed in neuron pairs.
source: In summation, our findings illuminate a discernible negative correlation between the probability of synaptic connections and the similarity level of γ-PCDH isoforms expressed in neuron pairs (Figure 4E).
evidence: The claim is supported by correlation analysis data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: The more similar the patterns of γ-PCDH isoforms expressed in neurons, the lower the probability of synapse formation between them.
source: Simply put, the more similar the patterns of γ-PCDH isoforms expressed in neurons, the lower the probability of synapse formation between them (Figure 4F).
evidence: The claim summarizes the main finding and is supported by the data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: 5' end single-cell sequencing data provided solid evidence for the combinatorial expression pattern of γ-PCDH isoforms in neocortical neurons.
source: Our 5' end single-cell sequencing data provided solid evidence for the combinatorial expression pattern of γ-PCDH isoforms in neocortical neurons.
evidence: The claim is supported by the single-cell sequencing data presented in the results section.

claim: The absence of γ-PCDH significantly increased functional connectivity between adjacent neocortical neurons.
source: Firstly, the absence of γ-PCDH significantly increased functional connectivity between adjacent neocortical neurons.
evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiological recording data from Pcdhg cKO mice.

claim: Electroporation-induced overexpression of identical γ-PCDH variable isoforms in developing neurons markedly decreased their connectivity.
source: Secondly, electroporation-induced overexpression of identical γ-PCDH variable isoforms in developing neurons markedly decreased their connectivity.
evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiological recording data from overexpression experiments.

claim: Increasing the similarity level of γ-PCDH variable isoforms expressed in neurons led to a reduction in their synaptic connectivity.
source: Lastly, using sequential in utero electroporation with different batches of isoforms, we found that increasing the similarity level of γ-PCDH variable isoforms expressed in neurons led to a reduction in their synaptic connectivity.
evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiological recording data from sequential electroporation experiments.

claim: γ-PCDHs regulate the specificity of synapse formation by preventing synapse formation with specific cells, rather than by selectively choosing particular targets.
source: These findings suggest that γ-PCDHs regulate the specificity of synapse formation by preventing synapse formation with specific cells, rather than by selectively choosing particular targets.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the combined results showing that similarity in γ-PCDH expression reduces connectivity.

claim: Stochastic and combinatorial expression patterns of cPCDH have been identified in Purkinje cells.
source: Stochastic and combinatorial expression patterns of cPCDH have been identified in Purkinje cells (Esumi et al., 2005; Toyoda et al., 2014) and olfactory sensory neurons (Mountoufaris et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: In serotonergic neurons only one isoform, Pcdhac2, has been mainly detected.
source: However, it is noteworthy that in serotonergic neurons only one isoform, Pcdhac2, has been mainly detected (Chen et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a previous study (Chen et al., 2017).

claim: cPCDH diversity and the presence of ubiquitous C-type expression are not universal features throughout the brain.
source: These diverse observations across different cell types suggest that cPCDH diversity and the presence of ubiquitous C-type expression are not universal features throughout the brain (Kiefer et al., 2023).
evidence: The claim is inferred from observations across different cell types and supported by a citation.

claim: 5' end single-cell sequencing detected more isoforms in individual cells compared to SMART seq results from the Allen Institute's database.
source: Furthermore, compared to the SMART seq results from the Allen Institute's database (Tasic et al., 2018) and others (Lv et al., 2022) focusing on γ-PCDH, 5' end single-cell sequencing used in our study not only detected more isoforms in individual cells but also revealed more neurons expressing C-type isoforms.
evidence: The claim compares the current study's results with previous studies using different sequencing methods.

claim: Neurons from the neocortex of Pcdhg knockout mice exhibited significantly more dendritic spines.
source: Previous studies by Molumby et al. demonstrated that neurons from the neocortex of Pcdhg knockout mice exhibited significantly more dendritic spines, while neurons overexpressing a single γ-PCDH isoform had fewer dendritic spines in Molumby et al., 2017.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a previous study (Molumby et al., 2017).

claim: The absence of the whole cluster of cPCDH affected synaptic connections among lineage-related cells.
source: Tarusawa et al. revealed that the absence of the whole cluster of cPCDH affected synaptic connections among lineage-related cells (Tarusawa et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a previous study (Tarusawa et al., 2016).

claim: Overexpression of the C-type γ-PCDH isoform C3 showed a negative effect on synapse formation within a defined clone.
source: More recently, overexpression of the C-type γ-PCDH isoform C3 also showed a negative effect on synapse formation within a defined clone (Lv et al., 2022).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a previous study (Lv et al., 2022).

claim: The connection probability between excitatory neurons lacking the entire cPCDH cluster in layer 4 was approximately twofold higher at early stage P9–11, significantly lower at P13–16, and similar to control cells at P18–20.
source: Tarusawa et al. demonstrated that the connection probability between excitatory neurons lacking the entire cPCDH cluster in layer 4 was approximately twofold higher at early stage P9–11, significantly lower at P13–16, and similar to control cells at P18–20 compared to Tarusawa et al., 2016.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a previous study (Tarusawa et al., 2016).

claim: Pcdhg-/- pyramidal neuronal pairs consistently exhibited a higher connection probability from P10 to P20.
source: In our study, Pcdhg-/- pyramidal neuronal pairs consistently exhibited a higher connection probability from P10 to P20.
evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiological recording data from the current study.

claim: γ-PCDH might have different functions in neurons located in layer 2/3 compared to layer 4.
source: Secondly, γ-PCDH might have different functions in neurons located in layer 2/3 compared to layer 4.
evidence: The claim is speculated based on differences observed between the current study and previous studies.

claim: Only variable, but not C-type isoform C4, had a negative impact on synapse formation.
source: However, our study demonstrated that only variable, but not C-type isoform C4, had a negative impact on synapse formation.
evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiological recording data from the current study.

claim: Distinct C-type isoforms may play varied roles in shaping neural networks within the brain.
source: Building upon previous findings, it is becoming increasingly evident that distinct C-type isoforms may play varied roles in shaping neural networks within the brain (Garrett et al., 2019; Steffen et al., 2023; Meltzer et al., 2023; Lv et al., 2022).
evidence: The claim is inferred from multiple previous studies cited.

claim: The similarity level, rather than the absolute expression of the protein, affects synapse formation between neurons.
source: These observations suggest that the similarity level, rather than the absolute expression of the protein, affects synapse formation between neurons.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the sequential electroporation experiments.

claim: The interplay between γ-PCDHs and neuroligin-1 plays a crucial role in the negative regulation of dendritic spine morphogenesis.
source: Previous studies have established that the interplay between γ-PCDHs and neuroligin-1 plays a crucial role in the negative regulation of dendritic spine morphogenesis (Molumby et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a previous study (Molumby et al., 2017).

claim: The overexpression of multiple γ-PCDH variable isoforms in one neuron only affected its connection if the other neuron overexpressed an identical combination of γ-PCDH isoforms.
source: Our findings also demonstrated that the overexpression of multiple γ-PCDH variable isoforms in one neuron only affected its connection if the other neuron overexpressed an identical combination of γ-PCDH isoforms.
evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiological recording data from sequential electroporation experiments.

claim: The diversified combinatorial expression of γ-PCDHs plays a pivotal role in neurons selecting their synaptic partners in the mouse neocortex.
source: This highlights the pivotal role of the diversified combinatorial expression of γ-PCDHs of neurons in selecting their synaptic partners in the mouse neocortex.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the combined results of the study.

claim: Overexpressing six variable isoforms resulted in a reduced connection rate in Pcdhg cKO mice.
source: Notably, while the overexpression of the γ-PCDH C4 isoform had no discernible effect on synaptic connectivity, overexpressing six variable isoforms resulted in a reduced connection rate in Pcdhg cKO mice.
evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiological recording data from overexpression experiments in cKO mice.

claim: Variable isoforms, as opposed to the C-type isoform C4, play a critical role in synapse formation within the mouse neocortex.
source: These observations underscore the critical role of variable isoforms, as opposed to the C-type isoform C4, in synapse formation within the mouse neocortex.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the combined results of overexpression experiments with variable and C-type isoforms.

claim: The absence of γ-PCDHs causes significantly more synaptic formation among neocortical pyramidal neurons.
source: Furthermore, while the absence of γ-PCDHs causes significantly more synaptic formation among neocortical pyramidal neurons, evidence supports that their absence also leads to a significant reduction of synapse formation in other brain regions.
evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiological recording data from the current study and contrasted with findings in other brain regions.

claim: Mice lacking γ-PCDHs exhibit fewer synapses in spinal cord interneurons.
source: For example, mice lacking γ-PCDHs exhibit fewer synapses in spinal cord interneurons (Weiner et al., 2005) and diminished astrocyte–neuron contacts in co-cultures from the developing spinal cord (Garrett and Weiner, 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Knocking down γ-PCDHs causes a decline in dendritic spines in cultured hippocampal neurons.
source: Knocking down γ-PCDHs causes a decline in dendritic spines in cultured hippocampal neurons (Suo et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a previous study (Suo et al., 2012).

claim: The absence of γ-PCDHs leads to reduced dendritic arborization and dendritic spines in olfactory granule cells.
source: The absence of γ-PCDHs leads to reduced dendritic arborization and dendritic spines in olfactory granule cells (Ledderose et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a previous study (Ledderose et al., 2013).

claim: Immuno-positive signals for γ-PCDHs are more frequently detected in mushroom spines than in thin spines.
source: Additionally, immuno-positive signals for γ-PCDHs are more frequently detected in mushroom spines than in thin spines (LaMassa et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a previous study (LaMassa et al., 2021).

claim: The absence of γ-PCDHs had a more pronounced impact on vertically aligned neurons than on horizontally situated pairs in the neocortex.
source: Moreover, our observations revealed that the absence of γ-PCDHs had a more pronounced impact on vertically aligned neurons than on horizontally situated pairs in the neocortex.
evidence: The claim is supported by electrophysiological recording data from the current study.

claim: Different mechanisms may be employed by synapses in different brain regions to achieve their specificity.
source: These findings suggest that different mechanisms may be employed by synapses in different brain regions to achieve their specificity.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that γ-PCDH absence has different effects in different brain regions.

claim: Different mechanisms have been proposed for targeting specific inhibitory neural circuits in the neocortex, including 'on-target' synapse formation for targeting apical dendrites and 'off-target' synapse selective removal for somatic innervations.
source: Notably, different mechanisms have already been proposed for targeting specific inhibitory neural circuits in the neocortex, including 'on-target' synapse formation for targeting apical dendrites and 'off-target' synapse selective removal for somatic innervations (Gour et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a previous study (Gour et al., 2021).

claim: The similarity level of γ-PCDH isoforms between neocortical neurons is critical for their synapse formation.
source: In summary, our data demonstrate that the similarity level of γ-PCDH isoforms between neocortical neurons is critical for their synapse formation.
evidence: The claim summarizes the main finding of the study.

claim: Neurons expressing more similar γ-PCDH isoform patterns exhibit a lower probability of forming synapses with one another.
source: Neurons expressing more similar γ-PCDH isoform patterns exhibit a lower probability of forming synapses with one another.
evidence: The claim summarizes the main finding of the study.

claim: The presence of γ-PCDHs enables neocortical neurons to choose which neurons to avoid synapsing with, rather than selecting specific neurons to form synapses with.
source: This suggests that the presence of γ-PCDHs enables neocortical neurons to choose which neurons to avoid synapsing with, rather than selecting specific neurons to form synapses with.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the combined results showing that similarity in γ-PCDH expression reduces connectivity.

claim: The unique expression pattern of clustered protocadherins (cPCDH) leads to millions of possible combinations of cPCDH isoforms on the neuron surface.
source: The unique expression pattern of clustered protocadherins (cPCDH) leads to millions of possible combinations of cPCDH isoforms on the neuron surface (Kaneko et al., 2006; Esumi et al., 2005), effectively serving as a distinctive barcode for each neuron (Yagi, 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The absence of γ-PCDH does not induce general abnormalities in the development of the cerebral cortex, including cell differentiation, migration, and survival.
source: Notably, the absence of γ-PCDH does not induce general abnormalities in the development of the cerebral cortex, including cell differentiation, migration, and survival (Wang et al., 2002; Garrett et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: γ-PCDH presence has been detected at synaptic contacts.
source: However, γ-PCDH presence has been detected at synaptic contacts (Fernández-Monreal et al., 2009; Phillips et al., 2003; LaMassa et al., 2021), and its absence has substantial effects on neuronal connectivity (Tarusawa et al., 2016; Kostadinov and Sanes, 2015; Lv et al., 2022).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The homophilic properties of γ-PCDH promote dendritic complexity.
source: While the homophilic properties of γ-PCDH promote dendritic complexity (Molumby et al., 2016), emerging evidence suggests that it might hinder synapse formation.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a previous study (Molumby et al., 2016).

claim: Homophilic interactions, facilitated by large overlapping patterns of cPCDH isoforms on opposing cell surfaces, may lead to intercellular repulsion.
source: Previous studies indicate that homophilic interactions, facilitated by large overlapping patterns of cPCDH isoforms on opposing cell surfaces, may lead to intercellular repulsion (Rubinstein et al., 2015; Brasch et al., 2019; Honig and Shapiro, 2020; Lefebvre et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The absence of γ-PCDH results in significantly more dendritic spines and inhibitory synapse densities in neocortical neurons.
source: Consistent with the repulsion concept, the absence of γ-PCDH results in significantly more dendritic spines and inhibitory synapse densities in neocortical neurons (Molumby et al., 2017; Steffen et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Neurons overexpressing one of the γ-PCDH isoforms exhibit significantly fewer dendritic spines.
source: Paralleling this, neurons overexpressing one of the γ-PCDH isoforms exhibit significantly fewer dendritic spines (Molumby et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a previous study (Molumby et al., 2017).

claim: The absence of the clustered PCDH augments local reciprocal neural connection between lineage-related neurons in the neocortex.
source: Furthermore, the absence of the clustered PCDH augments local reciprocal neural connection between lineage-related neurons in the neocortex (Tarusawa et al., 2016; Lv et al., 2022), even when sister cells exhibit more similar expression patterns of γ-PCDH isoforms (Lv et al., 2022).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Each neuron expresses multiple isoforms of γ-PCDH.
source: It is important to note that each neuron expresses multiple isoforms of γ-PCDH (Kaneko et al., 2006; Lv et al., 2022).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The combinatorial expression of γ-PCDHs empowers neurons to decide which partners to refrain from forming synapses with, rather than merely determining which ones to engage in synaptogenesis with.
source: Through multiple whole-cell patch-clamp recordings after the sequential in utero electroporation, we discovered that the combinatorial expression of γ-PCDHs empowers neurons to decide which partners to refrain from forming synapses with, rather than merely determining which ones to engage in synaptogenesis with.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the results of sequential electroporation experiments.
